newsitem.title: USA: Gateway 2000 sees smaller revenue gain.
newsitem.headline: Gateway 2000 sees smaller revenue gain.

text.p: Gateway 2000 Inc Chief Executive Ted Waitt said Tuesday that the company's revenue increase from the third quarter to the fourth quarter in 1996 will not be as strong as it was between the same quarters in 1995, when revenue jumped 50 percent.

However, Waitt told investors at the Montgomery Securities Tech Week conference that Gateway 2000's fourth quarter will be strong this year, declining to give further details. He added that personal computer sales to consumers remain strong in the fourth quarter, despite signs of a slow Christmas season for the rest of the industry.
"November was a good month for our major corporate accounts, but the primary growth has come from consumers," Waitt said.
Gateway 2000 specializes in selling mail-order PCs. The company has so far avoided a disappointing Christmas season as some PC makers who sell through retailers are experiencing.
"We probably won't grow at that sequential rate this year," he said referring to the increase from the third to fourth quarter last year.
"In '96 there wasn't as much new technology driving the market," Waitt said adding that fourth quarter revenue will be above the year ago quarter but he declined to offer specific forecasts.
Despite the slower sequential revenue growth, Gateway 2000 is expected to report one of the strongest earnings in the PC industry, said Montgomery Securities analyst Kurt King.
"Based on what was said today, my estimates for the December quarter would be too low," King said, adding he expects earnings per share of $1.00 for the December quarter.
In the fourth quarter a year ago Gateway earned $0.74 a share.
